units.translation: You will not get less than you deserve (I wrote this instead of ἀξίως [worthily]).

About the garment in which Agamemnon was wrapped by Clytaemnestra: ἐν πέπλοισιν μελαγκέρῳ λαβοῦσα μηχανήματι τύπτει [having caught him in robes, she strikes with a black-horned device]. In M there is written above: μελάγκερων [black-horned]. The scholiast explains both. The strange epithet is explained by the fact that the words ἄπεχε τᾶς βοὸς τὸν ταῦρον [keep the bull away from the cow] preceded; on this see Hermann's note and Wecklein in Aeschylean Studies p. 2.
τὰν ναύστολον μελάγκροκον θεωρίδα [the ship-borne, black-sailed sacred embassy]. I corrected this from τὰν ἄστονον μελάγκροκον ναύστολον θ [the un-groaning, black-sailed, ship-borne...].
with a black army (μελαγχείμῳ [black] in M)
for it is heavy with white and black fates

Figuratively of a gloomy mind, Pers. 114 μελαγχίτων φρήν [black-cloaked mind], where Blomfield says: "with a stronger metaphor he wanted to express the Homeric φρένες ἀμφιμέλαιναι [blackened wits] Il. 1,103; 17,83."
No hope of fear walks in my house, where Weil reads οὔ μοι μελάθρων ἐλπὶς ἐμπατεῖν φόβον [no hope of fear walks in my halls].
coming to the halls and hearth-homes
I will go to the halls of the house
No one forbidding keeps me from the halls
removing the mutual-slaughtering madness from the halls
the porch of the royal halls
by rubbing and blows it becomes black and compact, having been justified

The black-aegis Erinys does not leave the house (Brunck reads δόμους [the houses]), which the scholiast explains as μελαιναν αἰγίδα φορούσα [wearing a black aegis]. Thus the Erinyes are called μελανείμονες [black-clad] at Eum. 375. The faulty accent μελαναιγίς in M was corrected by L. Dindorf in the Thesaurus vol. 5 p. 715 from Etym. M. p. 518, 54.
